literal: Natural sharpness of intellect along with book-learning to those who possess, exceedingly subtle obstacles what are there before them to stand?
translation: For those who possess natural sharpness of intellect along with deep learning, what obstacles are so exceedingly subtle that they can stand before them?
modern: இயற்கையான அறிவு நுட்பத்தையும் அதனோடு நூல் அறிவையும் உடையவர்களுக்கு, அவர்களுக்கு முன்னால் வந்து எதிர்க்கக்கூடிய மிக நுட்பமான சூழ்ச்சிகள் அல்லது தடைகள் எவை உள்ளன?
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme capability of an ideal minister who combines natural intelligence with acquired learning. The term 'mati-nuṭpam' refers to innate, sharp intellect, while 'nūlōṭu' emphasizes that this must be paired with the study of authoritative treatises. For a person endowed with both, the poet asks rhetorically what 'ati-nuṭpam' (exceedingly subtle or complex obstacles) could possibly stand in their way. Their combined wisdom easily penetrates and resolves even the most intricate challenges.
